question: Does neuronal WWOX restoration started AFTER symptom onset recover any endpoint, or only prevent one when given in the neonatal window?
why_now: Every partial-benefit lever in this module is ordered as a bridge to, or a substitute for, restoration; whether restoration works after onset decides which of those two framings is the real one, so one result re-reads the whole list.
evidence_available: WWOX-system, read beyond the abstract: the high-dose arm reaches a survival plateau to day 300 and lowers spike-wave discharges to a wild-type-indistinguishable level; glucose and weight endpoints are prevented. Every treated arm was injected in the stated neonatal window.
evidence_depth: E4 - card reviewed, 12 WWOX-side assertion(s) read beyond abstract; class pharmacology table (IT7 P5)
decisive_uncertainty: No arm exists in which treatment begins after the phenotype is established; the window is stated, not measured against a later start, and P300 readouts are survivor-selected.
next_test: One added arm of the published design with injection after the first recorded spike-wave discharge, same endpoints, untreated same-genotype comparator kept.
feasibility: Established model and established vector; the added arm is a timing change, not a new assay.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: the two gene-addition cards (C01, C04) and their assertion rows; the deepdive manifest of the source; the work-order statements for this need. Checked for a post-onset arm and found none. Not a statement about the literature beyond the sources this module has read.

question: Before any ISR-attenuating compound can be ordered: in a WWOX-deficient HUMAN neural system, does the ISR run high or low?
why_now: The need's direction is unresolved and the two available readouts disagree by design, so no compound on this axis can be qualified either way. Resolving the sign is the cheapest act that converts the largest blocked slice of the catalogue into an orderable or a refused question; leaving it unresolved keeps that slice invisible rather than negative.
evidence_available: WWOX-system transcript-level only and contradictory: the knockout organoid shows the ISR target set lower, one shRNA library per arm shows it higher, and the designs are not comparable. No ATF4 protein and no eIF2-alpha phosphorylation measurement exists in the sources read.
evidence_depth: E3 - card reviewed with assertions; no WWOX-side result read beyond abstract
decisive_uncertainty: Which sign the ISR actually has at protein level in a WWOX-deficient human neural cell. Until that is measured, an ISR-attenuating compound and an ISR-potentiating compound are equally defensible, which is the definition of an unqualified axis.
next_test: ATF4 protein and eIF2-alpha phosphorylation by immunoblot in a WWOX-deficient human neural line against an isogenic control, one differentiation stage, no compound involved.
feasibility: A protein measurement on material the module already reasons about; no new model and no compound needed.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: this need's eleven observation rows and their readout levels; the ISR card and its assertions; the search layer over the eight ISR targets (78 associations, 56 families, none direction-coherent because the need direction is unresolved). The gap is a missing measurement in the sources this module has read, not a claim about the ISR literature.

intervention: T-type calcium blockade, isoform-discriminating set (efonidipine, flunarizine, against the carded T-type agents)
question: Which T-type isoform carries the suppression of the provoked seizure phase, and does the effect depend on the genotype?

Two approved compounds with different isoform reach make the discrimination possible without building a tool compound, which turns a standing caveat into a measurable question.
evidence_available: WWOX-system: a T-type blocker suppressed the late phase of the provoked seizure score in the null mouse, one experiment, genotype specificity not established by an interaction. next_test: The published provoked-seizure design with a drug-by-genotype interaction term and the isoform-discriminating pair beside the carded agent; identical provocation and scoring.

intervention: NMDAR antagonism (the carded tool compound and the clinically used class)

evidence_available: WWOX-system: blocking NMDAR abolished the burst in the WWOX-deficient slice, one drug, one preparation. The recording bath magnesium is not stated in the source, and the incubation solution already contains magnesium.
evidence_depth: E4 - card reviewed, 1 WWOX-side assertion(s) read beyond abstract; class pharmacology table (IT7 P5)
decisive_uncertainty: Whether a partial, clinically achievable block suffices, and whether the carded effect is a subunit effect or a pore-block effect. A pore blocker's potency depends on voltage and on magnesium, so the unreported bath is itself the obstacle.
next_test: Repeat the slice burst assay with the magnesium concentration reported, a partial-block agent beside the tool compound, and the untreated same-genotype comparator.
feasibility: The slice preparation exists; the change is a reported bath and one added arm.
novelty_perimeter: Queried: this need's eight observation rows, the two NMDAR cards and their assertions, and the search layer over the eight receptor-subunit targets (709 associations, 187 families). next_test: Measure the axonal activity-dependent myelination signal in the WWOX-deficient system against an isogenic control, before any compound; then decide whether the class is orderable.
